subject: Mutual Action Plan — Launch Gate: Network Smoke & Egress Playbook
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@medivance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch Gate: Network smoke & egress checklist (initial)

Alex —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. To keep the activation on schedule, here’s a concise mutual action plan focused on the network and security validations we need before we move traffic to the Private deployment. Please review and reply with owners/dates for items you own. I attached our onboarding template for reference.

High-level asks (owner / due):
- Service account + IAM: provide a scoped service account for our runtime to call KMS and push logs (Medivance IT / 5 business days)
- VPC CIDR and peering details: confirm the VPC CIDR and whether you want a VPN or private peering (Medivance Net / 3 business days)
- Egress allowlist: list of external destinations Redwood will need to reach (KMS endpoints, metrics, S3-buckets) — see sample attached (Medivance Sec / 3 business days)
- Static IPs or NAT: do you require static outbound IPs for our egress? If so, provide public NAT IPs or announce preferences (Medivance Net / 3 business days)
- Firewall rules: confirm L4/L7 ingress rules. Our runtime needs TLS port 443 and optional healthcheck ports.
- KMS integration: confirm KMS key ARN and rotation policies (Medivance Sec / 5 business days)
- Audit logs and retention: SLA for delivery of VPC flow logs and audit exports (Medivance Sec / 5 business days)
- Sample traffic window: propose 2-hour window for smoke tests and telemetry verification (both teams / agree by EOD)

Preflight checks we’ll run from Redwood side during smoke:
- TCP connectivity to runtime endpoints (443)
- TLS handshake and cert validation (mutual TLS if enabled)
- KV cache warmup with synthetic tokens
- Tokenized sample requests (10 tenants @ 50 qps burst)
- Egress flow verification to the allowlist

Attachments: redwood_onboarding_template.xlsx (template with exact fields), egress-allowlist-sample.txt

If you can reply with the names and a proposed 48-hour window for sample traffic by EOD tomorrow we’ll schedule the runbook and reserve an engineer.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Customer Activation
Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai

From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@medivance.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medivance Ops <ops@medivance.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch Gate: Network smoke & egress checklist (initial)

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching our network summary and a quick sketch of our perimeter (medivance_network_summary.pdf). Quick answers up front:
- We prefer a site-to-site VPN for now. VPC CIDR is 10.20.0.0/16.
- We can provide a NAT gateway with two static egress IPs (54.233.77.12, 54.233.77.13).
- KMS: we use AWS KMS; key alias is alias/medivance-data. Rotation policy is 365 days.
- Audit logs: we can stream flow logs to the Medivance S3 account; retention 13 months.

Questions from our security team:
1) Is mutual TLS supported for control-plane calls, or do you expect only server-side TLS?
2) For sample traffic, can you confirm that tokens used are synthetic (non-PII) and that logs are scrubbed?
3) Will Redwood provide an allowlist template with exact FQDNs/IPs?

We can do a smoke window Wed 13 May 2026 10:00–12:00 PT. Please confirm if that works and who will be on the call from Redwood for immediate troubleshooting.

—Alex
Alex Tan
Head of IT Operations
Medivance
alex.tan@medivance.com
+1 (206) 555-4222

Attachment: medivance_network_summary.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alex Tan <alex.tan@medivance.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Launch Gate: Network smoke & egress checklist (initial)

Folks — forwarding the Medivance responses. Key follow-ups for our side:
- Ben: confirm whether the runtime can support mTLS for control-plane calls and what config is required. Also, prep the allowlist template (FQDNs + IP ranges).
- Karthik: validate whether the NAT/static IPs pair fits our egress IP fingerprinting for downstream customers (we sometimes pin metrics origins).
- Kimberly: can you prepare the runbook and assign an on-call engineer for Wed 13 May 10:00–12:00 PT?

Alex — we’ll confirm owners in follow-up. Quoting your note below for context.

> On Mon, May 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM Alex Tan <alex.tan@medivance.com> wrote:
> Naomi —
> 
> Thanks for the clear list. Attaching our network summary and a quick sketch of our perimeter...

Thanks —
Naomi
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Tan <alex.tan@medivance.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch Gate: Network smoke & egress checklist (initial)

Naomi / team —

Short answers:
- mTLS: runtime supports mutual TLS for control-plane; we’ll need the client certs from Medivance (PEM bundle). If Medivance prefers server-only TLS we can run in that mode but will call it out in the security note.
- Allowlist template: attached (I’ll add FQDN examples and required ports).
- NAT IPs: the two static IPs they provided are acceptable. We’ll ensure egress mapping is consistent during smoke.

Kimberly — I can pair with you for the 13 May window. I’ll take the first hour to validate TLS handshakes and the second hour to run synthetic load and egress verification.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
ben@redwood.ai
